item.p: Engines: src/function_library_higher_order_internal.h declares three resumable engines defined in the higher-order part and used by all three parts: a traversal (one call per item, member or entry, with its position; for-each, filter, index-where, take-/drop-while, every, some, for-each-pair, array:build/for-each/filter/index-where/for-each-pair, map:for-each/filter), folds (fold-left/right, scan, array folds) and sorts (sort-by, sort-with, highest, lowest, array:sort/-by/-with). Keys are computed one call each, then sorted by sxml_evaluator_sort_indices; sort-with runs a bottom-up merge sort one comparator call per step. No engine calls a function item ().

Hidden rows: partially applied functions and fn:op's functions are function items whose body is a row no part lists (native operations, ): captured values hold the wrapped function, the bound positions and values, or the operator's code.

Types the front end lacks: the $keys of sort-by are map(*)* (the grammar has no optional or extensible record fields); the engine checks key, and order and atomizes key values itself. fn:partial-apply takes map(xs:integer, item()*) because map coercion does not relabel keys (an xs:integer key is not an xs:positiveInteger); a position below 1 is XPTY0004.

Placeholders: lowering turns $f(?) into fn:partial-apply with the empty map, so the empty map returns $function unchanged only for an anonymous function item; a map, an array or a named function is wrapped, so $m(?) is not a map (hof-920) and has no name (XPath 4.0, 4.5.2.5).

fn:function-lookup uses the dynamic context's function table; a row that needs the focus at that arity raises XPDY0002 at lookup (F&O 4.0 allows raising early), IR functions (XQuery) are UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.
Not yet: array:index-of (needs 1.20's deep-equal); a dynamic call on a sequence of functions (DynamicFunctionCall-146) is the evaluator's.
